title: Do Merging Black Holes Fire Off the Universe's Fastest Particles?
hook: Wrap a spinning black hole in a trillion-gauss magnetic field and particle collisions just outside its horizon reach energies we otherwise only see in the rarest cosmic rays.
key_points: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays carry ~10²⁰ eV, and their sources remain unidentified.
The Bañados-Silk-West mechanism lets particles collide near a spinning black hole's horizon at enormous energies.
The authors add magnetic fields of 10¹²–10¹⁴ gauss around merging binaries seen by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA.
Collision energies reach 10¹⁸–10²⁰ eV, squarely in the observed cosmic-ray range.
Below 10¹² G gravity dominates; above 10¹³ G the field boosts energies by nearly ten times.
Remnants with spin ≳0.85 and mass ≳100 solar masses top out near 10²⁰ eV.
content_html: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are the universe's most extreme particles, single nuclei carrying macroscopic amounts of energy, and nobody is sure what makes them. Carlos Coimbra-Araujo, Rita Anjos, Jonas Pereira and Jaziel Coelho nominate a candidate that has only recently become observable: the moments just before two compact objects merge.
extra_html: The engine they invoke is the Bañados-Silk-West mechanism, in which particles falling toward a rapidly spinning black hole can meet head-on just outside the horizon at collision energies far above what either brought in. The authors solve the charged-particle geodesics in magnetized Kerr spacetime, adding fields of 10¹² to 10¹⁴ gauss of the kind expected around neutron stars and merger remnants, and find center-of-mass energies of 10¹⁸ to 10²⁰ eV — the ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray range. Sweeping the parameter space turns up three regimes: below about 10¹² gauss gravity does all the work, between 10¹² and 10¹³ gauss gravity and magnetism compete, and above 10¹³ gauss the field amplifies collision energies by nearly a factor of ten. Applying this to the 34 gravitational-wave events with rapidly spinning remnants, they find that systems with spin above roughly 0.85 and masses above about 100 solar masses reach the full 10²⁰ eV. The appeal of the proposal is that it is checkable: gravitational-wave catalogs already supply the masses and spins, so the predicted particle energies follow.

related.title: The Amaterasu Particle Might Not Be a Proton
related.hook: One of the most energetic cosmic rays ever caught hit Earth with the energy of a thrown brick — packed into a single particle. New work says it may be a heavy nucleus, not a proton.

related.title: A Galaxy That Makes Neutrinos Without a Black Hole
related.hook: Astronomers expected a feeding black hole behind a flood of cosmic neutrinos. Instead they found furious star formation — hinting dusty starburst galaxies seed the high-energy neutrino sky.

related.title: 390 Gravitational Waves In, and Black Hole Astronomy Is Just Getting Started
related.hook: The latest gravitational-wave catalog leaps to 390 confirmed detections — including the clearest signal ever caught and evidence some black holes are built from earlier mergers.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.

flashcards.prompt: What role does the magnetic field play in this acceleration scenario?

choices.text: Above ~10¹³ G it amplifies collision energies by nearly an order of magnitude over gravity alone
It confines the particles so they never escape the merger
It replaces gravity as the only source of acceleration at all field strengths

flashcards.explanation_html: The authors find three regimes: below 10¹² G the field barely matters, 10¹²–10¹³ G is a transition, and above 10¹³ G magnetic effects dominate and boost energies nearly tenfold.

flashcards.prompt: Which merger remnants reach the very highest energies in this study?
flashcards.back_html: Those with high spin and large mass — dimensionless spin ≳0.85 and mass ≳100 solar masses — reach maximum energies around 10²⁰ eV.

flashcards.prompt: Why is linking gravitational-wave events to cosmic rays attractive?

choices.text: GW data measure the remnant's mass and spin, giving testable predictions for the energies reachable
Cosmic rays and gravitational waves arrive at the same moment from the same direction
It proves cosmic rays are made of gravitons

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper computes maximum energies for real detected events using their measured masses and spins — turning gravitational-wave observables into quantitative cosmic-ray predictions.
